name: St. Anton am Arlberg
kurzbeschreibung: The cradle of alpine skiing: St. Anton am Arlberg offers 301 kilometres of pistes in Ski Arlberg, over 200 km of deep snow and legendary après-ski.
beschreibung: St. Anton am Arlberg lies at 1,304 metres at the end of the Stanzertal valley in Tyrol and is regarded as the cradle of alpine skiing. The Ski-Club Arlberg was founded here as early as 1901, the first ski race took place in 1904 and in 1921 Hannes Schneider opened the first ski school. Today, together with St. Christoph and Stuben, the village forms the eastern part of Ski Arlberg, Austria's largest connected ski area. It offers 301 kilometres of pistes, more than 200 kilometres of deep-snow variants and 85 lifts and cable cars. The Valluga, with its viewing platform at 2,811 metres, is the highest point. The Arlberg-Kandahar races, the mass-start race Der Weisse Rausch and the lively après-ski are legendary. In summer, hiking, biking and the Arlberg Trail are the main attractions.
